title: SDK Integration Walkthrough — Laguna Retail
summary: Walkthrough of Redwood SDKs (Python & TypeScript), auth patterns (API key vs SSO), environment setup and quickstart examples. Covered hosted vs dedicated considerations and security requirements from Laguna's side.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-18 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Arjun Kapoor (Redwood SE), Sam Torres (Laguna CTO), Priya Sharma (Lead Engineer), Ethan Cole (Security)

[00:00] Jordan Lee: All right, hey everyone thanks for hopping on. I'm Jordan from Redwood, this is Arjun our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:05] Sam Torres: Doing well, thanks. We wanted to focus on the SDK integration today — our eng team will be doing the POC next week.
[00:10] Arjun Kapoor: Great, we'll go through Python and TypeScript quickstarts, auth patterns, env setup, and then show a tiny demo calling the hosted API and mention Dedicated options for later.
[00:22] Priya Sharma: Quick note — security will need info on KMS and audit logs, Ethan's here to ask questions.
[00:28] Ethan Cole: Yep, SOC2 questions too, and we need to understand how secrets are stored and rotated.
[00:32] Jordan Lee: Perfect, we'll cover that. Arjun, do you want to kick off with the Python quickstart?

--- Python quickstart / auth ---
[01:10] Arjun Kapoor: Sure. So with the Redwood Python SDK you pip install redwood-inference in your venv, set an env var REDWOOD_API_KEY and then a simple call looks like:

    from redwood import Client
    client = Client(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY'])
    resp = client.generate("Summarize latest order data")

(there was a small screen share, some code windows)

[02:05] Priya Sharma: Do you recommend storing the key in plain env or vault? We use Hashi and AWS Secrets Manager.
[02:12] Arjun Kapoor: We recommend secrets manager or vault for production; env var is fine for dev. The SDK will accept passing a token directly or using the REDWOOD_API_KEY env var. For rotation we integrate with customer KMS if you self-host private control plane, or Redwood managed KMS for hosted with HSM-backed keys upon request.
[02:30] Ethan Cole: When you say managed KMS, what level of control do we get? Audit logs?
[02:35] Jordan Lee: Yes, we produce audit logs for API calls and key usage, can push logs to your S3 or Splunk, and we have SOC 2 attestation. We'll share the security pack after this call.

--- TS quickstart ---
[03:10] Arjun Kapoor: TypeScript quickstart is similar: npm i @redwood/inference then use the client:

    import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'
    const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })
    const res = await client.chat.create({ messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Extract intents from this message' }] })

[03:45] Sam Torres: Any difference in streaming support between SDKs? We stream responses to the UI.
[03:52] Arjun Kapoor: Both SDKs support streaming. In TS you'll use an async iterator or event callbacks; in Python we have an iterator-based stream API. Perf is equivalent on hosted. For Dedicated you can tune concurrency and batching.

--- Env setup & quickstart repo ---
[04:30] Jordan Lee: We'll share our quickstart repo link: <https://redwood.ai/quickstarts/sdk> with example env files. For local dev we recommend a .env file with REDWOOD_API_KEY set, then use a secrets manager in CI and prod — we'll provide a Helm chart snippet if you go on-prem.
[04:55] Priya Sharma: Can you show multi-env config for staging vs prod? We have different API keys per environment.
[05:05] Arjun Kapoor: Absolutely — set REDWOOD_ENV=staging and use separate keys. Our SDK supports explicit client configs: new Client({ apiKey, baseUrl }) so you can point staging to a dedicated staging endpoint if you request Dedicated pools.

--- Auth patterns & SSO ---
[06:00] Ethan Cole: We use SAML SSO and want RBAC controls for who can call LLMs. Can Redwood integrate with our IdP?
[06:08] Jordan Lee: Yes, Redwood supports SSO (SAML/OIDC) for the console and admin plane. For programmatic API calls you still use API keys or mTLS tokens; we can issue short-lived tokens from your IdP via a broker pattern. For Dedicated/Private customers we support SCIM and group mapping so you get role-based access.
[06:30] Ethan Cole: Ok, so engineers wouldn't embed long-lived keys in repos?
[06:34] Arjun Kapoor: Correct — use short-lived tokens, vault, or instance profiles. We'll include example CI workflows that fetch a token and call the SDK.

--- Hosted vs Dedicated discussion ---
[07:05] Sam Torres: We're considering hosted first then Dedicated if latency/cost profile needs it. Thoughts?
[07:12] Arjun Kapoor: That's a common path. Hosted is quickest to start and gives you access to our model catalog. Dedicated gives predictable throughput, reserved GPU pools, and private networking. For low-latency edge cases we can route by region and provide autoscale controls.
[07:30] Priya Sharma: For our POC we care about token cost and 99th percentile latency under 5s. Can you run a small benchmark?
[07:38] Jordan Lee: Yes — we can run a benchmark on a representative prompt set. Arjun will coordinate. We'll need a sample prompt file and expected concurrency.

--- SDK internals & batching ---
[08:10] Arjun Kapoor: Quick note on batching — the SDK will send batches when there's queueing on the client side; you can configure batch size and timeout. If you care about latency you can set smaller batch windows. We also support prefix/KV cache on the runtime to reduce repeated context cost.
[08:35] Sam Torres: You mentioned KV cache — is that customer controllable?
[08:39] Arjun Kapoor: On Dedicated/Private you can control cache TTLs and pre-warm specific prefixes; hosted has safe defaults but you can request tuning for high volume.

--- Security deep-dive (short) ---
[09:10] Ethan Cole: A couple more security items: data residency, encryption at rest, E2E in-flight encryption, and audit retention.
[09:18] Jordan Lee: We encrypt data at rest and in transit, you can choose region pinning for hosted. For Private deployments you control the storage and keys. Audit retention is configurable; we can export logs to your SIEM. We'll send the SOC 2 and ISO docs.
[09:35] Ethan Cole: What's the recommended approach for PII scrubbing?
[09:39] Arjun Kapoor: We recommend pre-processing on your side to redact PII before sending, or use our redaction hooks in the SDK which can automatically mask common patterns — we'll share the pattern list.

--- Live demo: quick code run ---
[11:00] Arjun Kapoor: I'll run a tiny example: calling chat.generate with a sample user query, streaming tokens back and then writing to stdout. (short pause) Sample output — some tokens stream in, small latency ~200ms per token in hosted region us-west.
[13:20] Priya Sharma: Nice. Can we plug this into our Next.js front end?
[13:25] Arjun Kapoor: Absolutely, the TS SDK has a browser bundle and we show an example of streaming via web sockets or SSE in the quickstart. Keep keys out of the browser — use a backend token exchange.

--- Questions and common objections ---
[15:00] Sam Torres: What's the fallback if a model is down or capacity is exhausted?
[15:05] Jordan Lee: We do smart routing and fallback to compatible model variants — you can define fallback policies per route in the Console. Also, we have graceful degradation strategies like reduced response lengths.
[15:20] Priya Sharma: How do you measure quality regressions during rollout?
[15:25] Arjun Kapoor: Redwood Optimize ties model rollouts to evals and prompt sets; you can set regression alerts and auto rollback. We'll share an example eval config.

--- Recap & next steps ---
[17:00] Jordan Lee: To recap: we'll send the quickstart repo, security pack, a sample benchmark plan, and a POC checklist. Arjun will coordinate the benchmark and Priya will provide the prompt file.
[17:18] Priya Sharma: I'll share prompts and concurrency targets by EOD tomorrow.
[17:22] Jordan Lee: Great, we'll aim to have a Benchmark run scheduled next week.

Transcript notes: occasional transcription errors (Arjun's name sometimes shows as "Arjun Kapoor (Support)" in the auto transcript), minor mis-heard product names (e.g., "Redwood Dedicate" instead of "Redwood Dedicated"), filler words preserved.
